when wealth is given, human beings, ancestors, and gods are all fully satisfied. (89)
Thus concludes the ritual for consecration.

For one who has abandoned attachment to wealth, the accomplishment [of consecration] according to the path of the Jina’s teaching is achieved through the nine-fold salutations and the *sūra-mantras*; this is the exclusive teaching [of the Buddha]. (90)
The planets and all-knowing deities are established upon the footstool;
by that infinite variety, the path to liberation has been proclaimed. (p. 41) || 91 ||
Wherein the mothers of the Jinas, as well as the Yakṣiṇī Gautamī, have attained perfection;
thus the twenty-four forms (mūrtis) have arisen throughout the three times.
Thus, in the practice of the Jinas, one should establish a three-walled house, as well as a temple with a pinnacle, such as the Aṣṭāpada and others. (93)
A palace that brings happiness to one free from passion should be constructed in the center of the city;
one should likewise arrange it for a group of virtuous people in the four directions.
Thus ends the consecration of the Jina.
The construction of ponds, wells, and the like is prescribed during the five months beginning with Māgha;
for a large tank (taḍāga), one should perform it during the four months of Āṣāḍha and Mārgaśīrṣa.
O gods, the ancestors do not drink unconsecrated water; they attain satisfaction through consecrated water. Therefore, one should perform the consecration.
That man who creates a reservoir of water for the sustenance of trees and living beings,
or provides one, shall obtain happiness on earth and in heaven.
Formerly, during the slaying of Andhaka, sweat fell from the forehead of Rudra onto the earth;
from that, an exceedingly unbearable being was produced.

Having been suddenly seized by the gods and placed face-down upon the ground, its knees were in the southeast (Agni) corner, its feet in the southwest (Nairṛta) direction, and its head in the northeast (Śiva) direction. || 99 ||
Fifty-four deities reside within the body of the Vāstu;
eight goddesses are situated outside of them, and because they dwell [there], it is called Vāstu.
When the gods of the Thirty-three have made their petition with faces cast downward, the Bali offering is performed;
by that very offering one brings about peace, otherwise there is ruin.
When beginning or renovating palaces, mansions, and the like, or in all architectural works, [the deities] being worshipped shall bestow happiness. (102)
From a single word up to a thousand words, there may be thirty-two maṇḍalas, and their forms shall correspond to the [specific] field. (103)
Whether the site consists of eighty-one squares or sixty-four squares,
one should worship two mandalas in all divisions of the site.
Īśa is on the head; Parjanya has taken refuge in the right ear;
Jaya is on the shoulder; and Mahendra and the other four reside in the five fingers of the right arm. (105)
Mahendra, Sūrya, Satya, Bhṛśa, and Ākāśa, as well as Vāyu, Pūṣan, and the others, are stationed at the knees; seven are situated on the soles of the feet. || 106 ||
Pūṣan, Vitatha, Gṛhakṣata, both Yama and Yamī, Gandharva, Bhṛṅgarāja, and Mṛga—these are the seven deities. || 107 ||
Therefore, the ancestors reside upon the soles of the two feet;
moreover, Sugrīva is the gatekeeper, and Puṣpadanta is the lord of the waters.
The Asura, Śoṣa, and Pāpa, as well as the disease (Roga), are situated in the knee;
Ahi, Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Soma, and Sarpa are located in the two arms.
Aditi is situated in the lower region, and Diti resides in the left ear;
the thirty-two external deities are located there, while Brahmā (Vidhi) is stationed at the back of the navel.
Aryaman is on the right breast, while Pṛthivīdhara is on the left;
Vivasvat and Mitra are both upon the right and left thighs respectively. || 111 ||
Rudra and Rājayakṣman, along with Āpavatsa, are stationed in the heart;
likewise, Sāvitra and Savitṛ reside in the right hand.
Indra is in the penis, Indrajaya is on the left hand, Bhadra is also right there, and Bhadradāsa is likewise; such is the body composed of the gods. 113.
Carakī is in the northeast, Piliṃpiccha is outside in the east, Vidārikā is in the southeast, and Vijṛmbhā is situated in the direction of the waters (the west). 114.
One should worship Pūtanā in the southwest, Skanda on the shoulder [of the altar], Pāparākṣasī in the west, and Aryamā in the northwest; indeed, one should worship them everywhere. (115)
An offering to Heruka and the others should be made with black gram rice, liquor, and meat;
and other offerings should consist of *vaṭaka* cakes, all scented with gold.
Thus ends the ritual placement of the Vāstupuruṣa.
Without a second scripture that possesses superior qualities, the realization of the subject matter cannot be achieved through a single one alone.
Therefore, having observed from another perspective,
even one who is rich in the qualities of a jewel still desires assistance.
By the great grace of Śrī Viśvakarman Gaṇanātha, Maheśa Caṇḍī, and Śrī Viśvarūpa Jagadīśvara,
he fashioned this beautiful ornament for the temple.
Śrī Maṇḍana is the preeminent architect among the virtuous on earth.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Ornamentation of Temples," in the *Vāstuśāstra* composed by Śrī Sūtradhāra Maṇḍana. || 8 ||
Thus ends the "Adornment of the Palace."
